title: Waterlines in Flux: Aerial Hydrology of the Rhine Basin
author: Youth Media Lab // Integrational e.V.
summary: Documenting extreme seasonal water level fluctuations along the Rhine River using drone orthomosaic imaging, examining climate resilience measures and riparian wetland restoration.
content: Over recent decades, European inland waterways have faced unprecedented climate pressures — from prolonged summer low-water events stalling shipping corridors to flash-flood surges impacting alluvial ecosystems. Through the Green Horizon aerial monitoring program, young participants investigate how drone sensors can track shoreline recession, sediment shifts, and the vitality of restored floodplains along the Middle Rhine valley.
highlights: Orthomosaic aerial mapping of alluvial gravel bars
Thermal infrared assessments of heat stress in riparian foliage
Youth interview with regional hydrological monitoring engineers

title: The Shrinking Salt Flat: Drone Perspectives on Central Anatolia
location: Tuz Gölü Basin & Konya Closed Basin
author: Youth Media Lab // IESA
summary: Exploring the rapid hydrological changes of Lake Tuz and the Konya Closed Basin through high-altitude aerial sweeps, highlighting flamingo nesting sanctuaries and agricultural groundwater depletion.
content: Lake Tuz, one of the world's most unique hypersaline wetland biomes and a vital breeding ground for the Greater Flamingo, is witnessing severe climatic drying cycles exacerbated by changing precipitation patterns and intense irrigation. Using regulated drone flights, Turkish youth teams record high-contrast aerial textures of salt crusting, water boundaries, and fragile flamingo habitats to formulate compelling visual calls for sustainable regional water governance.
highlights: High-contrast aerial documentation of receding saline shorelines
Visual assessment of seasonal flamingo nesting zones
Grassroots youth advocacy dialogues with local agricultural communities

title: Canopy Guardians: Monitoring Virgin Forests in the Carpathians
author: Youth Media Lab // Asociația Empower Plus
summary: Deploying aerial imaging across steep mountain valleys to monitor primeval beech forest canopies, bark beetle infestations, and intact wildlife migration corridors.
content: The Carpathian Mountains harbour some of Europe's last remaining old-growth and virgin forests. Climate heating has rendered these majestic ecosystems increasingly vulnerable to drought stress and subsequent pathogen outbreaks. Romanian youth volunteers employ drone cameras to survey dense canopy health across inaccessible ridge terrain, contrasting pristine intact forest clusters with disturbed perimeter zones.
highlights: 360° aerial panorama capture for the Green Horizon VR Exhibition
Comparative visual inventory of old-growth versus fragmented forests
